locator.quote: OpenAI's construction attains $R(F)\ge Q(F)^{4-o(1)}$

feedback.feedback: The abstract leads with the one-family asymptotic form, while Theorem 1 states fixed-k estimates and the growing-k construction is relegated to an optional remark. These statements have different dependency chains.
feedback.why_it_matters: A reader cannot tell whether the main proof alone establishes the particular family advertised in the abstract.
feedback.advice: Identify the fixed-k optimal-exponent result and the separately supplied uniform schedule in the abstract’s scope, without importing its constants.
feedback.missing_bridge: Which of the fixed-k theorem and uniform growing-k consequence supports the displayed headline.
available_before: The title promises the total-function exponent four and the subtitle credits OpenAI.

locator.quote: the exact conditional sampler and the capped address predictor

feedback.feedback: The two named deliverables arrive before either the conditioned event or the predicted object has a plain description.
feedback.why_it_matters: The contribution sentence requires a specialist to retain two opaque technical labels until several later abstract sentences supply their roles.
feedback.advice: Tie each name to its output in place: a pivot drawn with the survival-weight law, and an address vector output under a fixed query cap.
feedback.missing_bridge: The sampled output, conditioning event and predictor output attached to their first names.
available_before: The title promises the total-function exponent four and the subtitle credits OpenAI.

locator.quote: address-hardness scale

feedback.feedback: The abstract introduces a hardness scale without saying what resource it measures or how it differs from the cost of decoding the entire r-bit address.
feedback.why_it_matters: A lower-bound reader cannot yet tell whether the factor m multiplies one-instance hardness, vector hardness, or the number of certificate bits.
feedback.advice: Describe the scale as a bit-query allowance below the randomized complexity of one partial-function instance; leave the symbol L to the body.
available_before: The abstract has introduced columns and addresses but no query allowance.
feedback.missing_bridge: One-instance hardness versus total address-query cost.

locator.quote: For fixed $k$

feedback.feedback: The fixed-parameter qualification is now present, but k has no referent anywhere in the abstract.
feedback.why_it_matters: The reader cannot tell whether k controls error, query count, dimension or the exponent.
feedback.advice: Identify k once as the Forrelation order or construction parameter when giving the fixed-k quantum cost.
feedback.missing_bridge: The mathematical role of k before the abstract uses it.
available_before: The abstract has named exact conditional sampling and a capped predictor as its contributions.

locator.quote: a true certificate can defeat every rival in a cheap comparison

feedback.feedback: The subject suggests that the comparator recognizes or checks a true certificate. The implemented comparison does not query any gate transcript.
feedback.why_it_matters: The distinction between pointer-based candidate selection and actual certificate checking is the mechanism that avoids nested search.
feedback.advice: Identify the winning column as the object being compared and say that the comparison only follows suggested pointers; defer validity checking to the later verification stage.
available_before: The introduction has described the exponent gap but not the input layout.
feedback.missing_bridge: Cheap pointer evidence versus certification of validity.

locator.quote: possibly in superposition over $i$.

feedback.feedback: The bit oracle is specified, but the free-gate convention is less explicit than the exactness arguments later require. Preparing an exactly uniform test index for arbitrary K and using exact reflections are harmless in query complexity, but they are not automatically harmless in a finite gate-set time model.
feedback.why_it_matters: The exact conditional-law claim should be understood in the intended oracle model before it is used as a proof invariant.
feedback.advice: Say once that arbitrary input-independent unitary computation and finite workspace are free, and that no gate-time or space bound is being claimed.
available_before: The preceding sentence says computation between queries is free.
feedback.missing_bridge: An explicit link from that cost convention to the exact unitary operations subsequently used.

locator.quote: A cap holds on every input and every branch, including branches on inputs outside the promise.

feedback.feedback: The all-input cap convention is imposed immediately after the standard R and Q notation without saying why it agrees with the usual promised-input convention. This is defensible, but the equivalence is part of the interface used later when a loser is decoded off promise.
feedback.why_it_matters: A specialist accustomed to a promise-restricted cost definition may wonder whether the paper has changed the complexity measure.
feedback.advice: Add the short cutoff justification: a purported promised-input cap can be enforced by terminating after that many queries, without changing promised-input behavior. Route the quantum padding detail to the model bridge.
available_before: R and Q have just been defined by success on the function domain.
feedback.missing_bridge: The equivalence between a domain-only cost convention and the enforced all-input cap.
